questions.question: Beneficiation means:
options: Processing raw materials into higher-value products before export — export the bakkie, not the ore
Selling raw materials at world prices

questions.question: A vehicle plant's BACKWARD linkages are:
options: The dealerships and mechanics that sell and service its vehicles
The suppliers it pulls into existence — component makers, transporters, toolmakers
Its debts to the development bank

questions.question: Why does a commodity-exporting economy need industrial diversification for STABILITY?
options: Its earnings ride the roller-coaster of world commodity prices, while a diversified base spreads risk across many products and markets

questions.question: The infant-industry caution warns that:
options: New industries should never be supported
Support without a finish line breeds industries that stay comfortable instead of becoming competitive, at consumers' expense

questions.question: South Africa's rolling industrial policy blueprints, under the 2007 framework, are the:
options: Industrial Policy Action Plans — the IPAPs, run by the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition

questions.question: The APDP supports the automotive industry by:
options: Rewarding local production and investment with import-duty credits and investment allowances

questions.question: The Industrial Development Corporation's role is to:
options: Set the repo rate for industry
Finance industrial projects that commercial banks find too slow or too risky

questions.question: Localisation through designated procurement means:
options: Factories may only hire local workers
Firms must relocate to rural areas
State entities must buy specified products — buses, rail stock, uniforms — from local producers, guaranteeing factories a market

questions.question: Left to the market, industry clusters in a few regions because:
options: Firms settle where suppliers, customers, ports and skills already are
Workers refuse to live outside Gauteng

questions.question: Apartheid's homeland decentralisation policy mostly failed because:
options: Incentives could not outweigh the absence of infrastructure, markets and skills — factories died when subsidies stopped

questions.question: The Maputo Development Corridor is:
options: A fenced industrial park in Gauteng
An SDI linking Gauteng's industry to Maputo's port through N4 road, rail and border upgrades in public-private partnership
A shipping route between Durban and Cape Town

questions.question: Which is a genuine part of the SEZ incentive package under the 2014 Act?
options: A reduced corporate tax rate of 15 percent, building allowances, employment tax incentives and duty-free inputs for export production

questions.question: The international best-practice recipe for industrial policy ties support to:
options: Export performance, keeps it temporary and conditional, and invests in skills and infrastructure alongside
Permanent protection of all local firms

questions.question: The single most damning aggregate fact in evaluating SA industrial policy is that:
options: Manufacturing's share of GDP has drifted down from over 19 percent toward 12 to 13 percent — deindustrialisation

questions.question: The binding-constraints test argues that:
options: Incentives should be doubled every year
Fixing electricity, ports, rail and skills may matter more than any subsidy, because incentives cannot compensate for failing networks

questions.question: 'Rands per sustainable job' is a criterion because:
options: Jobs cannot be counted any other way
It is required by the Constitution
Incentives spend public money, and a zone needing permanent subsidy repeats the homeland mistake in modern clothing

subtopics.title: The Bakkie and the Bag of Ore

questions.question: The bakkie earns far more than the bag of ore because:
options: Its price contains the wages, profits and taxes of every making step performed at home

questions.question: Hundreds of businesses 'hang off one assembly line' because:
options: Suppliers stand behind the plant and dealers and mechanics stand in front of it — the linkage web
Assembly lines are cheap to build

questions.question: Support for an industry 'must have a finish line' because:
options: An industry surviving only on protection is a permanent tax on everyone else, paid in higher prices

subtopics.title: Why the Factory Went to Coega

questions.question: The Coega package offers investors:
options: A ready-built zone with port, roads, power and water, plus 15 percent company tax, building help, hiring tax breaks and duty-free inputs for exporters
Free labour and free land forever
A monopoly on the South African market

questions.question: A corridor differs from a zone because it:
options: Wakes up a whole line of towns along a route, rather than one fenced site

questions.question: The homeland-factories lesson in one sentence:
options: You can pay a factory to arrive anywhere, but it only stays where business actually works

questions.question: Zones fail when they are:
options: Only a fence and a tax break in an empty field, without transport, power and skills fixed underneath

questions.question: A balanced evaluation of SA industrial strategy opens by:
options: Stating the test — help tied to exports, temporary, standing on working infrastructure and skills

questions.question: Which pairing correctly matches a named WIN with a named FAILURE?
options: The car programme failed; clothing thrived
The car programme and Coega's tenants as wins; collapsed clothing employment and empty-shed zones as failures
The Maputo Corridor failed; homeland factories thrived
Deindustrialisation as a win; vehicle exports as a failure

questions.question: The 'real bottleneck' move earns top marks because it argues:
options: That more sweeteners are always the answer
That incentives cannot outweigh power cuts, broken rail, queuing ports and scarce skills — so fixing foundations may beat any subsidy

questions.question: A defensible one-sentence verdict on SA's strategy is:
options: Everything failed and should be scrapped
Everything worked and needs no change
No verdict is possible in economics
The direction is right and the flagships earn their keep, but the strategy underperforms while the foundations crumble
